entities.name: A change is applied only once its checks have passed
entities.tagline: A change is applied to the model only once every check the model requires has passed on it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A check that can be skipped is advice; an instance's checks govern only where a change that fails them cannot land.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A change whose required check failed, or never ran, cannot be applied. Today the ruleset's required status checks meet it.

entities.name: A change is applied only to the state it was checked on
entities.tagline: A change is applied only on top of the state its checks ran on, so a change whose base has moved is checked again on the current state first.

follows: A state is read again before it is relied on

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Two changes that each pass alone can break the model together, and checks run on an older state say nothing about the state a change lands on.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A change whose base has moved cannot be applied until its checks have passed on the current state. Today the required checks in strict mode, with main merged into the branch, meet it.

entities.name: A change is applied whole or not at all
entities.tagline: A change is applied to the model whole, as one new state, or not at all.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: The checks hold the whole model, so a change applied in part leaves a state no check ever saw.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A change that fails while it is applied leaves the current state as it was. Today a merge commit meets it.

entities.name: A change is prepared apart from the model
entities.tagline: A change to any number of entities is prepared apart from the model's current state, unseen by its readers until it is applied.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: People and agents change the model at the same time, and a reader of the model, a server or a site must never see half a change.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Two changes edit the same entity and neither sees the other's edit before it is applied, and a reader of the current state sees neither. Today a branch, checked out in a worktree beside the clone, meets it.

entities.name: A change is shown entity by entity
entities.tagline: The difference between two states of a model is given per entity, per field and per section, with an entity paired across a rename by its id.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: The checks on a change compare an id, a decision's text and a label on either side of it, and a reviewer reads what changed in each entity; a difference by lines or rows, or one that reads a rename as a deletion and an addition, shows neither.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Renaming an entity shows as one entity whose name changed, and editing one field shows that field and nothing else. Today git's difference with rename detection, read after the checker puts both sides in one form, meets it.

entities.name: A change keeps the record of how it was accepted
entities.tagline: Every applied change keeps its difference, its discussion, each check's result and who applied it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Whoever asks later why a change is in the model, a reviewer, an auditor or the KPI that counts merges past their checks, reads that record and nothing else.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A year after it was applied, any change shows what changed, what was said about it, what was checked and who applied it when. Today a pull request meets it.

entities.name: A change names a seat its phase lists
entities.tagline: A change authored by a seat is refused unless the phase it names lists that seat.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: The author of a change says which seat did the work, and that is true only where the seat is one the phase of the work lets do it.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A change by a seat the named phase does not list is refused when it is made and again before it is applied. Today the commit-msg hook and the seat check on each pull request meet it.

entities.name: A change that carries a secret is refused
entities.tagline: A change that carries a secret is refused before it is stored.

follows: A secret is never written into a repository

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A stored secret is published to everyone who can read the model, and from then on it can only be rotated.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A change carrying a key in a known form is refused, and a push past the refusal shows who made it and why. Today push protection meets it for the forms GitHub recognizes.

entities.name: A check reads nothing but the instance
entities.tagline: The checks over an instance read the instance's files and nothing else: no network, no filesystem beyond what they are handed, and no module but the readers they share with the parser.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: The same checks run in a site's build, in the instance's workflow and in the tooling's own suite, and they give the same findings everywhere only when nothing outside the files they are handed can change the answer.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: The checker's functions take a map of path to text and make no network call; the same instance checked in its workflow and in a site's build at the same release gives the same findings.

rows: The meta-model, with what the checks are
The meta-model, with what the checks are

entities.name: A check's output is kept with the change it checked
entities.tagline: The output of every check run on a change is kept and can be read from that change.

follows: A check counts only when its output was seen

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A check counts as passed only when its output was seen, and the output is what a reviewer and every later reader hold a report against.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: The output of any check run on any applied change can be read from that change, its failures told apart from its notes. Today a check run's log, linked from its pull request, meets it.

entities.name: A check sees a change and the state it started from
entities.tagline: A check run on a change is given the whole proposed state and the state the change started from.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Some checks hold a change rather than its result, an id that changed, a decision rewritten, a label moved, a change's seat, and each of them needs both sides.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: The id check refuses a change that alters an id and passes one that does not, reading only what its run was given. Today `companygraph ids --range` over a pull request's base and head meets it.

entities.name: A check that passes says what it left
entities.tagline: A run of the checks that finds nothing still says what it did not check: every schema's writing rules, and any type its vendored core carries no schema for.

follows: A check counts only when its output was seen

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A check counts only when its output was seen, and a green run read as more than it is would let a page pass that nothing read. The writing rules are the agent pass's, and a run that said nothing about them would be read as having checked them.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A run with no finding passes and says that every schema's writing rules were not checked and are the agent pass's; a type the vendored core predates is reported as not checked; and an agent that cannot run the mechanical checks names them under Not checked rather than applying them by hand.

entities.name: A claim the evidence does not carry is marked before the answer ends
entities.tagline: After an answer's last sentence, each claim is read back against the tool answers that carried the entities it names, and every verdict reaches the page before the answer ends.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: An answer can name the right entity and say something about it the entity does not bear out, and the visitor deciding which sentences to trust needs that shown where they read, not in a report later. A verdict that arrived after the answer closed would mark nothing.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Given a claim whose verdict is carried in part, with a probability above the deployment's threshold, the page underlines the sentence, a note on hover or focus says so, a line under the answer says one claim was marked, and the kept line counts it; given a judge that does not answer within the check's budget, the answer ends as it would have and the kept line carries no count.

rows: A chat answer marks the claims its evidence does not carry
A chat answer marks the claims its evidence does not carry
The design, with what was measured
The design, with what was measured

entities.name: A fact no schema holds is written nowhere
entities.tagline: A fact a document or a page states that no schema has a place for is written nowhere in the model and noted nowhere beside it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A schema is the contract for what the model holds, and a fact slipped in beside it, a birth date, a revenue, a headcount, would be held by nothing and checked by nothing; naming it by kind tells the owner what was left out without writing down what they chose not to hold.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A CV that states a birth date yields a profile with the date written nowhere and a report that names a fact of that kind left out; a company page that states a revenue, a headcount, a funding round or a founding year as an age yields no extraction and no note of it.

rows: A profile is written from a person's documents
An agent does the work no script can, by the skills an instance ships
A profile is written from a person's documents
An agent does the work no script can, by the skills an instance ships

entities.name: A German reader reads the vocabulary pages in German
entities.tagline: The pages around the vocabulary read in Swiss Standard German when the reader switches to it, while the schemas the pages draw stay in the one language the model is written in.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: The person behind the family is Swiss, and a reader in Zürich or Bern is a reader the pages are written for. The schemas themselves are not translated, because a model is written in one language and a schema translated would be a second schema; that is the reason to depart, stated on the page beside the figure.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Switched to German, the model page around the figure and the stage's own labels read in Swiss Standard German, the schemas it draws stay in English, and the page says so beside them.

entities.name: A list arrives in pages that neither repeat nor skip
entities.tagline: A list of any length is answered a page at a time, and an agent that follows the cursor with the same arguments receives every result exactly once, in one order, every page naming the same commit.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: An agent passing a list on to a visitor cannot check it for gaps or doubles; the server has to make both impossible, and a page from another commit would mix two models into one list.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A search whose results run past one page, followed to its end, yields every result exactly once in one order with every page naming the same commit; and a limit of zero is answered with one entry and a page that says one was returned.

rows: Walk a long list a page at a time
Walk a long list a page at a time

entities.name: A model leaves its store as Markdown
entities.tagline: Any state of a model can be exported to the Markdown form with its ids, and imported back unchanged.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A company's model belongs to no tool, and the export is what lets it leave one; it is also what every check and every agent reads today.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A state exported and imported again is the same state, and the exported files pass `companygraph check`. Today the model is that Markdown.

rows: A vocabulary to describe a company in
A vocabulary to describe a company in

entities.name: A model that does not resolve is not served
entities.tagline: A commit at which a page names something that resolves to nothing is served by no surface: no graph is drawn from it and no page is published from it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A surface that served a broken model would hand a visitor a claim that leads nowhere, and the last commit that resolved is the better answer until the model is corrected.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A deployment built at a commit where a page names nothing draws no graph and serves nothing from that commit; and a site build at such a commit stops, says where the name was written and what it searched, and leaves the committed pages as they were.

entities.name: A move is shown before it is written
entities.tagline: A move of an instance to another release lists every path it would write or remove, and writes only on a yes.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A move touches the vendored core, the packs and the procedures, and an owner who sees the list first can stop a move that would reach a file they did not expect; a move that wrote first would leave the owner reading a diff to find out what happened.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Move a model, picked on an instance on an older release, lists every path before writing one, and the instance is moved only on a yes to Go ahead.

rows: An instance is made and kept from one command
An instance is made and kept from one command

entities.name: A name that resolves to nothing is reported with the type it searched
entities.tagline: The check reads every name a schema declares as a reference, and reports each one that resolves to nothing, with the type the declaration names and where the name was written.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A name resolves by the type its declaration names and never by a search over every type, so a writer told only that a name is unknown would look in the wrong folder; the type searched is what sends them to the right one.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A name that exists nowhere fails the page, saying what the column or field is declared to reference and that it names no entity; a name that exists under another type fails saying which type it is an entity of, and is never resolved there; and a name inside an owner resolves within that owner alone.

entities.name: A new instance passes its checks on its first day
entities.tagline: An instance the command writes passes the checks of the release that wrote it, with nothing in its model but the stubs.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A company that starts a model and meets a failing check before it has written a fact learns that the tooling, not the company, is what fails; the first run is where trust in the checks is won or lost.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A folder made with Make a model, checked at the release that made it, passes with no finding.

rows: An instance is made and kept from one command
An instance is made and kept from one command

entities.name: A page is checked as it is written by the gate's own checks
entities.tagline: A page is checked while it is written, by the same checker and the same schemas as the gate it will pass.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A writer who meets a failure only at the gate writes against the schema all day without seeing it, and a different checker in the editor would hold the page to a different model.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Before the change is proposed, an editor shows the failure the gate would report for the same page. Today the editor plugin, which bundles the checker at the instance's release, meets it.

rows: Checks while a file is edited
Checks while a file is edited

entities.name: A person's documents are used only under that person's consent
entities.tagline: Nothing from a person's documents or public pages is written into the model unless that person's consent is given, or the person is the owner modeling themselves.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A profile is written from CVs, diplomas and reference letters, and a company's instance from team pages that name people; each is a person's own, and a model that held facts about them without their word would be a second record of them they never agreed to. The owner's own documents need no one else's word, and asking would be noise.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Given documents of a person who is not the owner and whose consent is not given, the run writes nothing; given the owner modeling themselves, no consent is asked and the report says so in one line; and given a team page, a person whose consent is not given has their rows dropped and the run goes on without them.

rows: A profile is written from a person's documents
An agent does the work no script can, by the skills an instance ships
A profile is written from a person's documents
An agent does the work no script can, by the skills an instance ships

entities.name: A pin is moved only by its owner
entities.tagline: No pin a repository declares is moved by the machinery that reads it; a pin moves only in a commit the owner makes that says why.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A pin is editorial: a release or a commit behind is intent until the owner says it is drift, and a bot that moved pins would turn every upstream release into a change nobody decided.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A pins file whose tooling pin names a tag older than the upstream's newest is reported as behind, naming the newest tag, with nothing written and an exit of 0.

rows: A repository is held to one form and told which pins are behind
A repository is held to one form and told which pins are behind

entities.name: A pin that is behind is reported
entities.tagline: Every pin a consumer holds can be listed with how far it is behind what it pins.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A pin moves only on purpose, so whoever decides needs to see which are behind; a pin nobody sees is drift nobody chose.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: One command lists each consumer's pins and how far each is behind. Today `companygraph pins` and the family report meet it.

rows: A repository is held to one form and told which pins are behind
A repository is held to one form and told which pins are behind

entities.name: A published page is checked against the state it names
entities.tagline: Every page published from a model is checked against what the state it names would draw.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A page edited by hand, or drawn from another state, says something the model does not, and the model is corrected first and the page drawn again.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A page whose content differs from what its named state draws fails its site's check. Today `pages:check` and `build:check` in each site's required `verify` job meet it.

entities.name: A question is answered in the language of its words
entities.tagline: An answer is written in the language the message's words are in, and in the page's language only where the words do not tell.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A visitor is owed an answer in their words, and the page they are on is a weaker signal of their language than what they typed: a learner writing English on the German page wants English back. A German answer names each entity in Swiss Standard German first, with its exact title after, so the reader can both read the name and find the page.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A message in English words with German word order, sent from the German page, is answered in English; and a German answer written after a tool round names each entity in Swiss Standard German first with its exact title in parentheses after.

entities.name: A refusal carries a code a program can read
entities.tagline: A call the server refuses carries a code for a program beside the sentence for a reader, and the codes and the schema of a refusal can be asked for.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: An agent that is refused with a sentence alone has to guess what to do next, and a guess is where it repeats the call or gives up on a list it could have restarted. A code says which it is.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Every refused call carries a code; the tool that describes errors lists every code and the schema of a refusal; and a cursor from an earlier commit is refused with the code for an invalid cursor and the reason that it is from another commit, naming the commit now served.

entities.name: A released vocabulary never changes
entities.tagline: A release of the vocabulary, core or a pack, never changes once it is made.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: An instance adopts a release by naming it, and a release that moved would change the rules a model is held to without the model deciding.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: An attempt by anyone but the Owner to move or delete a released version is refused. Today a tag, held by the release-tag ruleset, meets it.

rows: A vocabulary to describe a company in
A vocabulary to describe a company in

entities.name: A shipped procedure is held to its hash
entities.tagline: Every procedure a release ships into an instance is recorded in the manifest with its hash beside the vendored core's, and a procedure edited in place fails the check by name.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: An agent asked for judgment work should follow the procedure its instance names and not one improvised or quietly changed; held to a hash like the vendored core, a procedure that drifted is found by the same check that finds a drifted schema.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: An instance written for an agent carries every procedure of the running release under the agent's skills folder with its hash in the manifest; a shipped procedure edited inside the instance fails the check on that file; and a procedure of the instance's own, under another name, is left alone by an upgrade.

rows: An agent does the work no script can, by the skills an instance ships
An agent does the work no script can, by the skills an instance ships

entities.name: A spent share refuses before the model is asked
entities.tagline: Once the hour's, the day's or the month's share the deployment wrote down is spent, a message is refused before any request to the language model is made.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A chat open to anyone who turns up spends money per message, and the ceiling is what lets the company leave it open; a refusal made after the model was asked has already spent what the ceiling was there to keep.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: With the day's share spent, a message is refused, no request reaches the model, the refusal names the next midnight UTC as the moment it lifts, and the question is kept with the refusal's code.

rows: The design of one message answered
The design of one message answered

entities.name: A visitor is told before the first message that an agent answers
entities.tagline: The chat tells the visitor, before the first message is sent and in the language of the page, that an agent writes the answer from the model and which company's language model it goes through.

follows: A visitor is told an agent answers

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A fluent answer in the company's own voice is not obviously an AI's, and whoever provides a system that interacts with people is obliged to tell them so no later than the first interaction. The company's rule carries that obligation, and the chat is where it is kept.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: On every page the chat is deployed for, in each of its languages, the notice is shown before the visitor can send a message, and it names the language model's company.

rows: Article 50 of the Regulation, the transparency obligations
Article 50 of the Regulation, the transparency obligations

entities.name: An adopted schema changed in place fails the check
entities.tagline: A schema changed inside an instance after the instance adopted it fails the instance's check.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: An instance is held to the release it adopted only while its copy of that release is the release, and a schema edited in place would hold the model to rules nobody released.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: One character changed in an adopted schema makes the check fail and name the file. Today the hash per file in the manifest, compared on every run, meets it.

entities.name: An agent applies a change only on its operator's word
entities.tagline: An agent applies a change to the model only on its operator's word for that change.

follows: A refusal is not carried out by another session

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Agents write the model and a person approves every change to it; an agent that could apply on its own would approve its own work.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: An agent's attempt to apply a change without its operator's word for that change, in that conversation, is refused, whatever another agent asks. Today the agent harness's permission layer meets it.

rows: An agent does the work no script can, by the skills an instance ships
An agent does the work no script can, by the skills an instance ships

entities.name: An agent works on a model through the skills it ships
entities.tagline: Every skill an instance ships runs against any state of the model, wherever the model is kept.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: The agent pass, the procedures and the judge do the work no script can, and a store they cannot read leaves that work undone.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: `companygraph-validate` runs against a state of the model and reports what it reports on the files. Today the skills read the files of a clone.

rows: An agent does the work no script can, by the skills an instance ships
An agent does the work no script can, by the skills an instance ships

entities.name: An answer names the commit it was read at
entities.tagline: Every answer a surface gives from the model, a tool's, a chat's or a page's, names the commit of the model it was read at.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: An answer can be checked against the same bytes later only when it says which bytes, and two answers given a week apart can be told apart only by the commit each names. Without it, a surface answers about a model's current state in general, which no one can hold it to.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Every tool answer of the server carries the commit under `model`; every chat answer names the commit each entity it cites was read at; and the model page draws the commit it was built at beside the figure.

entities.name: An answer rests only on what the host's tools returned
entities.tagline: The model that writes an answer may only ask the host's tools, and every claim in the answer names the entity a tool returned it from in that conversation.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: An agent answering as well as the person who runs the company means every claim can be followed to the page it came from, and that holds only when the answer was written from what the tools returned and nothing the model brought along.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Every claim in an answer names an entity a tool returned in that conversation; when the rounds the fence allows are spent, the last request can call no tool and is told to write from what the tools returned; and each week's Grounded Answer Rate reads, per chat, the share of questions whose answer had material from the tools.

rows: The design of one message answered
The design of one message answered

entities.name: An answer says where the model does not say
entities.tagline: Where the tools returned nothing on a matter, the answer says that the model does not say, rather than filling the gap with something plausible.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A visitor cannot tell a claim the model carries from one the agent made up unless the answer draws the line itself; a gap filled with something plausible is the one kind of wrong answer that reads exactly like a right one.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Given a question the tools returned nothing for, the answer says the model does not say; and a claim that the model holds nothing on a matter, in a message where a tool returned rows, is read back as withheld and counts as not carried.

rows: The design of one message answered
The design of one message answered

entities.name: An edited vendored file is overwritten only by force
entities.tagline: A vendored file that was edited inside the instance is never overwritten unless the move is forced, and a forced move names it as overwritten.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A vendored file is core's or a pack's to hold and never edited in an instance, but an edit someone made there is still their work; a move that overwrote it silently would lose the edit and hide that the instance had drifted from its release.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Given a vendored file edited inside the instance, a move writes nothing and names the file, a check fails naming the file as not as the tooling wrote it and says the forced upgrade puts it back, and a forced move overwrites it and names it as overwritten.

rows: An instance is made and kept from one command
An instance is made and kept from one command

entities.name: An entity keeps its id through every rename
entities.tagline: An entity carries one id for as long as it exists, through every rename and every language it is written in.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A page's name is what a reader sees and what the company may change; a system outside the model, a server's edge, a site's link or a test's citation, needs something that does not change when the name does. An edge that joined names would break on every rename, and a reader could not tell a renamed entity from a removed one.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A page renamed and the graph drawn again still has every edge joining the same id; and a commit that changes an id already on the default branch, a rename of it included, fails the range check a pull request runs.

entities.name: An instance is checked only against the release it adopted
entities.tagline: The checker that runs over an instance is the release its manifest names, and it reads the schemas from the core the instance vendored, so no release holds a model to rules it has not taken.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A release adds rules, and a company takes one when it decides to, in a commit that says why; a newer checker running over an older instance would fail pages for rules nobody there has read, and would make every release upstream a breaking change downstream.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A checker that is not the release the manifest names refuses before reading a page and says to move the pin and the workflow together; a manifest that vendors a core newer than the checker is refused with the same instruction; and a core tag newer than the release that runs is refused at init before anything is written.

rows: An instance is made and kept from one command
An instance is made and kept from one command

entities.name: An instance may make its own ids under a declared pattern
entities.tagline: An instance may declare a pattern its ids follow instead of the tooling's own format, and then the tooling only checks the ids and never stamps one.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A company that already issues identifiers, in a register or a ticket system, keeps them rather than carrying a second id beside its own; a tooling that stamped its own format over them would make every page carry two.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: With a pattern declared in the identifier page, the check holds every id to the pattern, and the backfill command refuses whole rather than writing an id of the tooling's own format.

rows: An instance is made and kept from one command
An instance is made and kept from one command

entities.name: Any past state can be read whole
entities.tagline: Any state a model has had can be read whole, by its id, for as long as the model exists.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A site and a server draw the model at the state they pin, and a check compares a change with the state it started from; both read a state that is no longer the latest.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A state from a year before is read by its id, and the checker finds in it what it found then. Today a checkout of a commit meets it.

entities.name: Applying a change keeps its author
entities.tagline: Applying a change keeps the author it was made with.

follows: A commit keeps the author it was made with

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: An author replaced by whoever applied the change would let a change made under a wrong identity reach the model looking correct, and would hide which seat did the work.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: An applied change shows the seat that made it, and apart from it the account that applied it. Today merging only with a merge commit, with squash and rebase turned off, meets it.

entities.name: Completion offers only the names the scope holds
entities.tagline: While a reference is typed, the editor offers exactly the names the declaration's scope holds: a field's type, and a row's owner where the row is scoped to one.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A name offered from the wrong type is a name the check will fail later; a completion that knows the declaration's scope cannot offer one, and the writer never has to know the vocabulary's folders to pick the right name.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A field declared as a reference to seats, when typed, offers the seats' names and no other type's; a row whose entity is scoped to an owner offers only that owner's names.

rows: Checks while a file is edited
Checks while a file is edited

entities.name: Every applied state has an id that names its content
entities.tagline: Every state of a model that changes were applied to has an id that names exactly that content and never any other.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A pin, a served answer and a published page each say which state of the model they come from, and that is worth something only while the name always means the same content.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Two reads of one state's id return the same content, byte for byte, at any later time, and a state that differs by one byte has another id. Today a git commit and its hash meet it.

entities.name: Every change says who made it and in which work
entities.tagline: Every change records its author, the person accountable for it, its time and the process, phase and track it was made in.

follows: A commit keeps the author it was made with

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: The seat check holds an author to a seat its phase lists, and a later reader asks who made a change and in which work; neither can be answered from a change that does not say.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A change without an author, a process or a phase is refused, and every applied change shows all of them. Today a commit's author, committer, date and trailers meet it.

entities.name: Every pass of the gate can be counted by week
entities.tagline: Every change applied, every required check gone past and every change of rights is kept in a log a scheduled job can read by week.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: The KPIs that measure the gate, Merges Past Their Checks and Change Fail Rate, are counted from that log and from nothing else.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A job that reads only the log counts a week's applied changes and the checks gone past as the KPI reports them. Today GitHub's audit log and rule suites, read by the weekly `kpi` workflow, meet it.

entities.name: Every surface says what the model says and nothing more
entities.tagline: Every surface that derives from a company's model, a page, a server's answer or a chat's, reports what the model says at one commit and adds no reasoning the model cannot show.

follows: Nothing claims what the model does not hold

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A visitor, a search engine and an agent should reach the same answer whoever asks, and that holds only when every surface derives from the one model the company keeps. A retrieval layer answers with a paraphrase that cannot be held to the evidence the model attached to the claim, and an inferred answer, however useful, is one the company cannot be held to.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: The same question put to the person who runs the company and to an agent reading its model gives two answers that agree, with the agent's followable to the page it came from; and the count of answers that name no commit is zero.

rows: The strategy that rules out a paraphrase and an inferred answer
The strategy that rules out a paraphrase and an inferred answer

entities.name: Going past a required check is recorded
entities.tagline: Every change applied while a required check had not passed is recorded with the check it went past and the account that applied it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A gate an admin can pass stays honest only where every pass is counted, and Merges Past Their Checks counts them.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Every change of a week applied past a required check can be listed with that check and that account. Today GitHub's rule suites meet it.

entities.name: No applied state is rewritten
entities.tagline: A state that changes were applied to is never rewritten or deleted.

follows: What is cited from outside the model is not rewritten

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Pins, answers and pages cite states by id, and a rewritten state leaves each of those citations pointing at something that now says another thing.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: An attempt to rewrite or delete a past state is refused and the refusal is recorded. Today the ruleset's refusal of a force push and of a deletion meets it.

entities.name: No call changes the model
entities.tagline: The server has no write path: no tool an agent calls changes the model, which moves only by a commit to its repository and a new pin.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A company serving its model to agents should not have to decide whether to trust one with changing it. A write path would make that decision for every company at once, and the model is corrected where it is mastered, in its repository, under the review every change there gets.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Every tool the server lists carries the annotation that it only reads, and no call made over the server's whole surface changes a byte of the repository it serves.

rows: The strategy, with what it rules out
The strategy, with what it rules out

entities.name: No level moves on new evidence without the owner's decision
entities.tagline: A claimed level in a profile is never changed by a document the agent read; a new level is proposed with the rows behind it and left as it is until the owner decides.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A level is a claim a person makes about themselves, and a document can show a skill without settling how well; an agent that moved the level on its own reading would put a claim in the person's voice that nobody made.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: On an update where a new document would change a claimed level, the reconciliation shows the level as a proposal with the rows behind it, and the page keeps the old level until the owner says otherwise.

rows: A profile is written from a person's documents
A profile is written from a person's documents

entities.name: Nothing a company writes passes through us
entities.tagline: A company's model, and the server and the chat that serve it, run in the company's own repository and cloud project from the parts we publish, so nothing the company writes passes through us.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A company that would have to hand over its model to be served has been charged for adoption, and an access layer that costs money is a seat count wearing a different name. What leaves the company's hands is only what a chat visitor sends, which goes to the language model the deployment names.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A deployment of the server and the chat names the company's own cloud project and the company's own key or project for the language model, and no request from either reaches a host we run.

rows: The strategy, where it runs and what leaves
The strategy, where it runs and what leaves

entities.name: Only named accounts apply a change
entities.tagline: A change is applied only by an account the company names for it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Applying a change is what makes it the model's, and who may do that is the company's decision.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: An account that may propose a change is refused when it applies one. Today the push restriction to the Owner's account meets it in an organization's repositories.

entities.name: The model changes only by applying a change
entities.tagline: The current state of a model changes only when a change is applied to it, never by a direct write.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Every guarantee the gate gives holds only for the changes that pass through it.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A direct write to the current state is refused for every account. Today the ruleset's pull request rule meets it.

entities.name: The pages leave the machine only on the owner's yes
entities.tagline: An instance's pages are sent to a service outside the machine only on the owner's yes to exactly the files, counts and digest shown for that run, and a yes given for another digest, an earlier run or another instance sends nothing.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Whether a company's pages go whole to an outside service is the owner's decision about their company's data, and it is a decision about these files and not about the judge in general. A run that sent on an earlier yes, or over a file list that changed after the yes, would send what nobody agreed to.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Run without the key, the judge sends nothing and prints the forecast and the digest; run with a digest that no longer matches what would be sent, it refuses; and the only run that sends is one given the digest the owner saw, with the key read from the owner's environment and never from the conversation.

rows: A decision model asks each page its schema's writing rules
A decision model asks each page its schema's writing rules

entities.name: The question is kept and the answer is not
entities.tagline: A chat keeps of each message one line, the question itself and whether the model could answer it, never with an address and never past ninety days, and keeps no answer.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: The one quantity the company watches is whether an answer rested on the model, and that is read from the question and the entities cited, not from the answer's text; an answer kept would be a record of a conversation the visitor was promised lives in their tab and ends with it.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: The kept line holds the question, its language, the entities the answer cited, how many tool calls were made and how many found nothing, and whether the fence refused, and no field holds the answer or an address; a line older than ninety days is gone.

rows: The interface, with the kept line's fields
The interface, with the kept line's fields

entities.name: The same content is stored the same way
entities.tagline: Two writers who make the same change store the same state, whichever editor each used.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A difference that is only form hides the change a reviewer has to read, and sets two writers disagreeing about nothing.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: The same edit made in two editors produces no difference between the two states. Today the one Markdown form, held by `companygraph form`, meets it.

rows: A repository is held to one form and told which pins are behind
A repository is held to one form and told which pins are behind

entities.name: Two edits of one entity are never merged silently
entities.tagline: Where two changes edit the same part of one entity, the second is refused until someone resolves the conflict.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: An edit lost without a word is a fact the model held and no longer holds, and nobody decided to drop it.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: Two changes edit one field of one entity, and the second cannot be applied until the conflict is resolved by hand. Today git's merge conflict meets it.

entities.name: Who may read a model is set for each model
entities.tagline: Each model can be read by exactly the accounts its company sets, by anyone where the model is published.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A company publishes one model and keeps another private, and that is never the store's to decide.

sections.heading: Fit criterion
sections.text: A model set private cannot be read by an account outside it, and a published one is read without an account. Today a repository's visibility meets it.

entities.name: A visitor takes an answer for a person's
entities.tagline: A visitor who asks the chat on one of our pages reads the answer as something a person at the company wrote to them.

threatens: The questions the AI Act asks a company are answered from its model

sections.heading: Cause
sections.text: The chat answers on the company's own page, in the company's own first person, fluently and in the language the visitor wrote in, and nothing in the answer itself says that an agent wrote it. What says so is a notice under the input, which a visitor may not read, or may read without learning from it that an AI is answering, because it names a product rather than saying the word.

sections.heading: Consequence
sections.text: The visitor holds the company to a sentence no person said, and the company has not told a person it meets that they were talking to an AI, which is the first thing the AI Act asks of a provider of such a system. The test the vision rests on, the same question put to a person and to an agent and the two answers compared, loses its meaning for a visitor who cannot tell which of the two they got.

entities.name: A branch is deleted only after its merge is confirmed
entities.tagline: A branch is deleted as a step of its own, once its merge is confirmed, and never chained after the merge.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A delete chained after a merge runs even when the merge fails, and deleting a pull request's branch closes it, so a merge that failed would lose the change it was meant to take.

entities.name: A change to what another repository vendors is released
entities.tagline: A change to what another repository vendors reaches it only in a release whose notes say what it asks of a consumer: a re-sync, a re-pin or more than either.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: What we make is taken as a tag with its notes, and a repository that vendors it moves to a later release only when it decides to. A change with no release has made every copy of it stale without telling anyone, and notes that do not say what a consumer must do leave each one to find out by breaking.

entities.name: A check counts only when its output was seen
entities.tagline: A check counts as passed only when its output, from a run over the change as it now stands, has been read; a report that it passed is not its output, and a check that finds nothing counts only once it has been shown to find something.

serves: Every gate an agent's work passes is held by a person

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A report is a claim, and the person or agent writing it is the one least placed to see what it missed, whether it comes from a seat of ours or from a contributor. A check run over an earlier state says nothing about the change as it stands, and a search that returns nothing may never have been asking the right question. The person at a gate decides on what the checks showed, so only an output, read, of a check that can find something tells us the change holds.

entities.name: A commit keeps the author it was made with
entities.tagline: A commit reaches the default branch under the author and address it was made with.

serves: Every gate an agent's work passes is held by a person

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Our history tells a contributor from a seat and a seat from the Owner by the author alone: on September 28, 2026 we decided that an agent's commit is authored by the seat it held, and a contributor commits under their own name. A squash re-authors a commit to whoever pressed the button, and a wrong identity lands looking correct. Merging with a merge commit, never a squash, is this rule, and so is never asking a contributor to commit as anyone but themselves.

entities.name: A refusal is not carried out by another session
entities.tagline: An action refused in one session, by the Owner or by its permission settings, is not carried out by another session, whatever the first session asks.

serves: Every gate an agent's work passes is held by a person

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A refusal is the Owner's decision. A session that does the refused thing for another bypasses it, and the history shows a change that passed a gate nobody approved.

entities.name: A secret is never written into a repository
entities.tagline: No key, token or password is committed to any of our repositories, in a file, a commit message or a test fixture; a secret lives in the store of the workflow or the service that reads it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Our repositories are public, so whatever is pushed is published the moment it reaches GitHub, and it stays in the history after a later commit removes it. A secret that reached a repository can only be rotated, never taken back, and everything it opened stays open until it is. For the same reason a secret is never printed, not even to check it: a value that reaches a transcript has to be rotated as well.

entities.name: A state is read again before it is relied on
entities.tagline: A state — a branch, a pull request, a check, a release, another session's work — is read again from its source in the conversation that relies on it; an earlier reading, or a session's transcript where the session can be asked, is not the state.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Several sessions and people move the same repositories at once, so a state read earlier in a conversation may have moved by the time it is acted on, and a transcript says what a session set out to do rather than what it did. Fetching main before a merge is this rule.

entities.name: A visitor is told an agent answers
entities.tagline: A visitor who asks a chat of ours is told, before the first message is sent and in the language of the page, that an agent writes the answer from the model and which company's language model it goes through.

serves: The questions the AI Act asks a company are answered from its model
motivated-by: A visitor takes an answer for a person's

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Article 50 of the European Union's AI Act obliges whoever provides an AI system that interacts with people to inform them that it does, no later than the first interaction, unless that is obvious from the circumstances; it applies since August 2, 2026, and reaches a company outside the Union whose system's output is used in it. Our chat is placed on our own pages under our own name on top of Anthropic's Claude, which makes us the provider of that system, and a fluent answer in the company's own voice is not obviously an AI's. The Act also asks that the text such a system generates be marked as generated in a form a machine can read; whether an answer streamed to a page and kept nowhere is such text is not settled, and this rule does not reach it until it is.

rows: Article 50 of the Regulation, the transparency obligations
Article 50 of the Regulation, the transparency obligations

entities.name: A worktree is removed only once its plan is done
entities.tagline: A worktree that holds a plan's ledger is not removed before every task of that plan is done, even when its pull request has merged.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A plan's ledger, its briefs and its task reports live in the worktree under `.superpowers/`, which git ignores, and `git worktree remove` deletes ignored files without asking, with or without `--force`, so nothing brings them back. A merged pull request does not finish a plan: a plan can carry tasks in other repositories that are still owed. Three ledgers were lost this way in September 2026, twice in one day.

entities.name: German follows reviewed English
entities.tagline: German is made only from English the Owner has reviewed, never from a draft.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A translation of a draft is translated twice: once now and again when the English changes under review, and the second time a sentence that moved in English is easily left behind in German. Translating once, from the reviewed text, makes the German follow a fixed text.

entities.name: No type enters core before an instance had to be written with it
entities.tagline: No type enters core before an instance has had to be written with it.

serves: Core holds a company without running out of vocabulary

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A schema reviewed by its author agrees with itself, so the only evidence that a type holds a company is a company being held by it. Since August 23, 2026 the vocabulary grows from companies actually being described in it, and a type asked for, specified or approved before any instance needed it would be a proposal shipped as vocabulary.

entities.name: Nobody is asked which company a request comes from
entities.tagline: Nobody who asks for vocabulary or tooling is asked which company they ask for, and a name they offer is not repeated.

protects: Describe the pattern, never the company

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A request is worth what it says about the shape a company could not describe, and that shape is the same whoever holds it. The vocabulary names no company it was drawn from, so knowing which one asked would only put a name where we have said none goes.

entities.name: Nothing claims what the model does not hold
entities.tagline: No specification, page or statement made for us claims a fact or a number about us or our work that the model does not hold; a fact about code, such as a command's flags, is taken from the repository that holds the code.

serves: An agent answers as well as the person who runs the company

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: The model is where a fact about us is mastered, entered only from prose we have already published and reviewed; a claim made anywhere else has neither, and a reader cannot tell it from one that does. Where a fact is missing, it is added to the model first, and then it can be said.

entities.name: One session holds a piece of shared work
entities.tagline: Before shared work — a release, a re-pin, a re-sync, a change across repositories — a session checks for open pull requests, branches and tags and asks the running sessions; the first to claim it holds it, says so, and tells the others when it is done, and no one else opens a parallel change.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Several sessions work in our repositories at once, and the Surveyor already works from the list of them and what each is doing, and Carry tells the sessions a change touches what changed. Without a claim made before acting, two sessions cut the same release or overwrite each other's branch.

entities.name: Personal data stays out of every model
entities.tagline: No model holds personal data about anyone but its owner describing themselves and the people who consented to be described in it.

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A model is published, read by agents and visitors, and kept in a history that never forgets a state, so personal data written into it could never be taken back. The records a company keeps about the people it serves, its customers, guests, patients and visitors, belong in the systems the model describes and never in the model itself; the model says that such a system holds them and what it does with them. The owner describing themselves, and a person who consented to a profile, chose to be in it.

entities.name: The model is corrected first
entities.tagline: Where something we publish — a page, a site, a release, an answer — disagrees with the model, the model is corrected first and the thing is rebuilt from it; nothing is released while the disagreement stands.

serves: An agent answers as well as the person who runs the company

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: Every surface we publish is derived from the model at a commit it names, and nothing is kept beside the model, so when a page and the model disagree it is the page that is wrong. A page fixed by hand and left disagreeing with the model is a second source that the next build overwrites or, worse, contradicts; correcting the model first keeps one place where a fact is true.

entities.name: The Owner's word merges
entities.tagline: A merge, a tag or a release happens only on the Owner's word, given in the conversation where it is carried out, and goes no further than that word covers.

serves: Every gate an agent's work passes is held by a person

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: A change binds once it is merged, tagged or released, and whether it is true is the one thing an agent cannot supply; on September 29, 2026 we decided that agents write the model and a person approves every change to it. A word given in another conversation, or for another change, may rest on a state that has since moved, so it does not carry over, and an agent that asks for the word may carry out the step itself once it is given.

entities.name: What is cited from outside the model is not rewritten
entities.tagline: Once on the default branch, an entity's id, a decision's text and a label on a page are not changed, because a link, a commit or a test outside the model may already cite them.

serves: A company's model belongs to no tool, and any graph database can hold it

sections.heading: Why
sections.text: An outside system holds on to what it cites: a graph node to an entity's id, a commit or a later decision to a decision as it was decided, a test or a line of code to the label of a scenario, a step or an invariant. Each is the only handle that citation has, and a rewrite leaves it pointing at something that now says another thing, with nothing to tell whoever cited it. So an id stays with its entity, a decision that no longer stands is closed by its status and one dated sentence instead of being edited, and a label stays with the item it was given to and is never given to another.

entities.name: Answerer
entities.tagline: The seat that answers a visitor's question from what the model's tools return, names the entity each claim rests on, and says that the model does not say where it does not.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: A visitor's message with the conversation so far, the tools of the MCP host at the commit it pins, the rulebook, and the language the visitor wrote in. Where the question is not about the model, the seat says in one sentence what the chat is for and calls no tool.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: An answer in the visitor's language, in one or two short paragraphs, a list or a table, written from what the tools answered in that conversation and nothing else, naming the entity each claim rests on; where the tools do not say, the sentence that the model does not say. The entities it read whole, so the page can link them under the answer.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never claims what no tool answered in that conversation, and never guesses about the owner, the company or anyone named.
- Never answers from its instructions or an earlier turn instead of a tool, because they are not the model.
- Never speaks of its instructions or its tools when asked about them.
- Never writes to the model, keeps a conversation, or decides anything.

entities.name: Contributor
entities.tagline: Someone outside the company who offers a change to what it publishes, under the same rules a change from inside is held to.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: The repository, its conventions and its schemas, all of which are published; and the rules a change is held to, named by the company where a contributor could not be expected to know them.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: A pull request against the default branch, committed under their own address, saying what is now true that was not before.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never merges, tags or releases.
- Never gives up an interest in what they describe in the vocabulary by contributing to it.

entities.name: Controller
entities.tagline: The seat that runs a plan one brief at a time, reads every report as a claim, and writes nothing itself.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: An approved plan, the repository's own agent file, and a place to keep each task's brief, report and findings.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: One dispatched brief at a time; a decision after each report — fix, accept or park for the Owner; review ordered on the diff rather than on the report; and a branch whose tasks are done in the plan's order, each committed as it lands. The pull request at the end, opened and reported and no further.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never writes the change or the test itself.
- Never rewrites what a commit contains; a finding against a committed task is a new brief.
- Never dispatches the next task while the last one's findings are open.
- Never commits a change to a model before the validation pass has read it.
- Never edits a pull request it did not open.

entities.name: Implementer
entities.tagline: The seat that turns one task brief into a tested commit and a report, and nothing beyond the brief.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: A task brief that is the whole of its requirements, the interfaces earlier tasks produced, the repository's own agent file and a path for the report. Where the brief is unclear the seat asks before starting.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: The change the brief specifies, test first where the brief says so; the commit in the git register; a report naming what was built, what was run and what it doubts; and a short status the Controller acts on.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never spawns a subagent or a reviewer; review comes from the Controller after the report.
- Never changes a test's expectation to make it pass.
- Never edits a pull request it did not open.

entities.name: Narrator
entities.tagline: The seat that speaks a talk's reviewed speaker notes, one clip per slide in each language, so the talk can be heard without its presenter.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: A deck whose speaker notes are reviewed in the language the clip is in, the cues the author wrote into them, and the voice and settings the rulebook names for that language. Where a note is not reviewed, the seat speaks nothing for that slide.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: One audio clip per slide and language, beside the deck it belongs to, stamped with what it was spoken from: the voice, the model, the settings and the text. A clip whose stamp still matches is left as it is.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never changes a word of the note it speaks, and never speaks text that is not on the slide.
- Never chooses its own voice, model or settings; the rulebook names them per language.
- Never speaks one language's note in the other language's voice.
- Never publishes a clip; the Owner listens to it first.

rows: Rulebook, with the ElevenLabs voices and settings
Rulebook, with the ElevenLabs voices and settings

entities.name: Owner
entities.tagline: The seat that decides what the project is for, says the last word on every page, and gives the word every merge, tag and release waits on.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: The model, read before deciding: the vision, the objectives and the strategies under them, and the values a decision is weighed against. A draft or a pull request to review, on the branch and on the rendered page. The signals a strategy names as showing whether it is working.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: Decisions, recorded where they bind: a merge, a tag, a release and its notes, a pin moved in a commit that says why, a corrected model. The reviewed English every translation is made from. The word that ends a question an agent has parked, and the word that closes a question the model has left open.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text: - Never approves a change a surface carries from the diff alone; the rendered page is read too.

entities.name: Partner
entities.tagline: The seat that shares the Owner's say in what the project is for and in how its work is shaped, specified, planned and implemented, and leaves to the Owner the word every merge, tag and release waits on.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: The model, read before deciding: the vision, the objectives and the strategies under them, and the values a decision is weighed against. A draft or a pull request to review, on the branch and on the rendered page. The signals a strategy names as showing whether it is working.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: Wherever a phase of Delivery, Contribution or Feature Request before Integrate names the Owner, the Partner may act in the Owner's place, and a phase's gate is passed by either word. Decisions at every gate before Integrate: a shaped request, an approved specification, plan or implementation, and reviewed English on a branch. A pull request the Owner can integrate. The word that ends a question an agent has parked.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never merges into the default branch, pushes to it or creates a release tag.
- Never approves a change a surface carries from the diff alone; the rendered page is read too.

entities.name: Planner
entities.tagline: The seat that cuts an approved specification into task briefs, each whole on its own, and writes none of them.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: A specification the Owner has approved, and the repository the work lands in, including the rules that bind it.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: An ordered set of task briefs. Each is the whole of its own requirements, names the interfaces the briefs around it produce and consume, and states how its holder can tell it is done. An entry of a model gets a brief of its own, because the Owner decides one entry at a time. The order is the order they can be worked in, not the order they were thought of.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never re-opens a decision the specification took.
- Never writes a brief that depends on a conversation its holder did not have.
- Never writes the change.
- Never plans a task whose completion cannot be checked.
- Never puts two entries of a model in one brief.

entities.name: Requestor
entities.tagline: Someone outside the company who could not describe something in the vocabulary, and says so where it can be answered.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: Whatever they were trying to describe and could not — the entity, the field or the rule that was missing when they stopped. Nothing else: the seat is filled by whoever turns up, and a request is not a form to be completed before it is heard.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: A GitHub issue on the repository the request concerns, in their own words, and a correction where the company restates it wrongly.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never has to know the vocabulary's terms to be understood; restating the request in them is the company's work.
- Never decides whether the gap is filled.

entities.name: Reviewer
entities.tagline: The seat that reads one diff against its brief, returns findings with a severity and changes nothing.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: The brief the work was done from, the implementer's report read as unverified claims, the diff as one file with its commits and context, and the constraints that bind the task.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: Two verdicts, spec compliance and quality, and findings each with a file and a line, what is wrong, why it matters and how to fix it, ranked by severity, with the strengths named first. Where the diff touched a model, a third verdict: every entity it touched read against its schema's writing rules, which no mechanical check reaches. A finding is an input to whoever merges and never a verdict: it does not decide, and it is not passed on a person.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never mutates the working tree, the index, a branch or the pull request.
- Never re-runs a suite to confirm a report; it runs one focused test on a doubt the report does not answer.
- Never reads a schema's writing rules as satisfied because the mechanical checks are green.
- Never spawns another reviewer.
- Never marks polish as critical.

entities.name: Specifier
entities.tagline: The seat that turns a shaped request into a specification nobody has to guess at, and builds nothing.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: A request already classified, the model and the vocabulary it must not contradict, and the code or the pages it will touch, read rather than remembered. Where the request is ambiguous the seat asks before writing.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: A specification that is the whole of the requirements: the gap it closes, the approaches considered with the one chosen and why, the decisions taken, and what is explicitly not being done. Where the change adds vocabulary, the instance that will be written against it. Where it reaches another repository, what its release will ask of a consumer. Where a decision is the Owner's, the seat names the options and parks the question.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never writes the change it specifies.
- Never decides scope; it names the options and the Owner chooses.
- Never specifies a type without naming the instance that will be written against it.
- Never leaves a question unasked because an assumption would be convenient.

entities.name: Surveyor
entities.tagline: The seat that finds out where all the open work stands at the moment the Owner asks, sets it out with one proposal for what comes next, and carries out only what the Owner then decides.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: The Owner's question, read access to every repository, pull request, branch and worktree of the company, the list of the other sessions at work and what each is doing, and the memory of what was settled before. Where it cannot read something, the seat says what it could not see instead of filling the gap.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: An overview checked at the moment of asking: what is open, in what state, and who is working on it, with each claim linked to where it was read. One proposal for what comes next and one decision put to the Owner at a time. On the Owner's word, that decision carried out, the other sessions told what changed, and a report of what happened, mistakes included.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never deletes or writes to the model without the Owner's word in that conversation.
- Never commits in its own name; a commit it makes on the Owner's word is made in the seat whose work it carries, under that seat's author and trailers.
- Never decides; where a choice is open, it proposes and the Owner decides.

entities.name: Translator
entities.tagline: The seat that makes the Swiss Standard German of an element whose English the Owner has reviewed, and hands back a back-translation beside it.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: The reviewed English of the elements the task names, and the glossary. Reviewed means the Owner has said the English is done; a draft is not reviewed, and the seat says so. Where the task names no elements, the seat names the gap and writes nothing.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: The German in the element's own place, de-CH in the forms Switzerland uses, and beside each element a back-translation in English, so a reviewer with a minute can read what the German says.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never edits the English.
- Never writes German into a model; a model is English, and the German a surface carries lives in the surface's own attributes.
- Never writes a family term in any form but the glossary's.
- Never commits.

entities.name: Visitor
entities.tagline: Someone who asks about the company in their own words, on its site or through an agent of their own, and is owed what the model says and nothing else.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: A question, in whatever words and language they have. Nothing else: the seat is filled by whoever turns up, and nobody is asked who they are.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: A question, and where the answer sends them, a click on the entity it rests on: on the model page, or on the file at the commit it was read from.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never has to know the model's vocabulary to be answered; meeting their words is the company's work.
- Never leaves anything behind: the conversation lives in their tab and ends with it.

entities.name: Writer
entities.tagline: The seat that drafts English in the family voice from a brief, so the Owner reviews a draft instead of writing one.

sections.heading: What it takes
sections.text: A brief naming the audience, the one point, the facts the text may claim and where each is shown, and the file and the place the text lands. The rulebook and the glossary. Where the brief lacks the audience, the point or a fact's source, the seat names the gap and writes nothing.

sections.heading: What it produces
sections.text: The text in its file on the current branch, in the register the place calls for, and a reply naming what was written, what changed and which claims could not be traced to the brief or the repository.

sections.heading: What it never does
sections.text:
- Never writes a fact the brief or the repository does not show.
- Never writes a count or a version of something that is still changing; it says where the number is read instead.
- Never writes German; the translation is the Translator's.
- Never commits and never runs the build.
- Never uses an adjective that sells.

entities.name: Chat answer
entities.tagline: The answer to a visitor's question, streamed as events to the chat panel on companygraph.io's pages, with each claim naming the entity it rests on and marked where that evidence does not carry it.

realizes: A chat answer marks the claims its evidence does not carry

rows: An interface description of the events an answer streams
An interface description of the events an answer streams

entities.name: MCP endpoint
entities.tagline: The Model Context Protocol endpoint at mcp.companygraph.io/mcp, where any agent client, and the chat, lists the types CompanyGraph's model declares, reads its entities and searches it, without signing in.

rows: The server's documentation, with the tools it exposes
The server's documentation, with the tools it exposes

entities.name: Governance research
entities.tagline: The research of October 14 and 15, 2026 on governance as data, kept in this repository under `docs/research/`: an inventory of every check the family runs, where it runs and on which level, and the requirements any store of a model must meet for those checks to keep governing it. It labels each requirement GD-01 to GD-40, and a requirement drawn from it carries that label as `source-id`. Nothing syncs from it: a requirement drawn from it is corrected on its page in this model, and the research stays the dated record it was drawn from.

entities.name: Local
entities.tagline: Written and kept in this repository, which masters every page in the model. Nothing syncs it, and it issues no identifiers, so no page carries a `source-id`.

entities.name: chat
